scope: Automatic scripture detection to browser selection, Preview, queue, and transcription Stop
reproduced_before_fix: When the single-verse lookup completed before chapter loading, the matching automatic selection was rejected as an operator change. John 3:16 remained in the number picker instead of the verse text list.
Background detections attempted to scroll while the Sermon browser was hidden. Returning to Sermon did not scroll the selected verse into view.
fixed: A matching selected book, chapter, verse, and translation from the parallel lookup now completes navigation instead of cancelling it. A different operator selection still cancels the delayed automatic selection.
Navigation tracks translation and explicit activation so translation changes and operator clicks on a pending background reference are handled.
Returning to the visible Sermon browser scrolls its selected verse row into view. The selected row exposes aria-current.
integration_boundary: Mounted real TranscriptPanel and ScriptureSearchTab, native event-listener bridge, real annotation/navigation actions, real Bible/Preview/queue stores, with controlled native verse/chapter IPC responses.
verified: John 3:16 opens its verse text list, selects and scrolls verse 16, stages the correct Preview, and queues the correct reference when verse lookup finishes first.
The same selection works when chapter loading finishes first.
Stop preserves the selected John 3:16 chapter, verse, reader, and Preview.
A background detection does not switch the active tab; returning to Sermon scrolls its selected verse.
An operator choosing a different verse during loading keeps that selected verse and Preview.
Changing translation during loading retains John 3:16 in the new translation and ignores the late old-translation response.
Clicking the same reference while its background chapter request is pending opens Sermon.
limits: This subagent did not control the native UI. The main agent performed and reported the optimized native app observations above.
A spontaneous chapter 3 to chapter 16 change was not reproduced. The final optimized native app correctly selected John chapter 3 verse 16.

Automatic Preview staging tests begin with empty Preview. The native run retained the deliberately staged note according to the existing operator-override policy; it does not establish automatic replacement of manually staged content.

native_optimized_release_verification.evidence_source: Actual native UI observations reported by the main agent; this subagent did not control the UI or read credentials.
native_optimized_release_verification.observation: Actual spoken John 3:16 opened John > Chapter 3, displayed the verse text list, and scrolled the selected verse 16 into view.

preview_policy.observation: Preview retained a manually staged Final release lines note. Program retained that note off air after its intentional Stop Live.
preview_policy.classification: Intentional operator override, not an incorrect John 16:16 preview.
preview_policy.source_behavior: Automatic detections use stageVerseInBackground, which fills empty Preview or replaces only its own previous automatic selection. It preserves operator-staged notes, songs, slides, verses, and timers. Explicit verse/reference clicks stage directly.
preview_policy.existing_regressions: src/lib/preview-staging.test.ts explicitly requires preserving a staged announcement, song, slide, verse, or timer.

stop.observation: After Stop sermon, the native UI showed Start transcribing and Start Sermon, both microphone meters were exactly zero, and Program was OFF AIR.

native_optimized_release_verification.additional_transcript_segments: Two ambient segments arrived after fixture playback while notes were being checked.

post_stop_tab_return.observation: A Songs to Sermon tab round trip retained John > Chapter 3 with verse 16 selected and scrolled into view. Six notes remained, with View Source enabled.
